# RETRO: PR #13216

## What worked
- One neutral brief to both reviewers; naming the dependency sources (Quickshell, Hyprland, systemd journalctl) in scope let both independently resolve the key "does journalctl exit after grep -m1" question from source instead of guessing.
- The central finding (lock-screen refusal consumes the one-shot watcher) was found independently by both reviewers.
- Cross-examination: two Opus-only claims (match scope across shells, missing journalctl stub in tests) were sent to Sol as neutral source questions; Sol confirmed both from source, so the public comment carries no single-sourced claim except the Opus-run test pass result, which is a sealed run.
- Editorial check passed on the first draft.

## Process deviations (candid)
- Opus reviewer (self-reported): host-side `python3 -c`/`jq` reads of `pr.json`, a python3 heredoc edit of its own fixture file, and `bash -n` on its own fixture script outside review.py. None touched PR code or the live session. All PR-related execution went through review.py (sealed run verified). Also read two files in parallel near the 60-line cap; lazy blob fetches in its own blobless dependency clones wrote under `opus/deps/` only.
- Sol reviewer (self-reported): three source reads exceeded the 50-line per-response bound (75, 55, 87 lines). No execution; evidence unaffected.
- Coordinator: one attempted Bash `sleep 240` status check was blocked by the harness (no execution); replaced with the background wait notification. Coordinator used host `jq`/`sed`/`python3` only to read intake metadata and build its own artifacts (no PR code executed). The Opus fixture script (426 lines) was not line-audited by the coordinator; public claims from it are limited to M1/M2/M3 observations that are also supported by source from both reviewers, and the refusal itself is source-established.
- Native memory: no supported session-local no-memory control was verified for the omarchy-reviewer subagent; its report contains no reference to prior-PR conclusions.

## Improvements
- Brief template: name the relevant test suites (`test/shell.d`) and ask reviewers to note which commands tests stub, since new background processes in production scripts can escape stubs.
- Coordinator tooling lacks a Markdown renderer; the HTML was produced by a small subset renderer. A shared renderer in review-team would reduce per-assignment code.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the diagnosis holds against dependency source, and the watcher restarts the shell as described on the normal path. One gap remains: a restart refused while the screen is locked is never retried. Two smaller notes follow.

| PR claim | Result |
|---|---|
| Hyprland drops a `socket2` client that stalls while events pile up | Confirmed in Hyprland source: once 64 events are queued for a client, it is removed and its socket closed ([`EventManager.cpp`](https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/blob/a0136d8c04687bb36eb8a28eb9d1ff92aea99704/src/managers/EventManager.cpp#L140-L167), v0.55.4; same logic in v0.56.2) |
| Quickshell 0.3.1 logs the error and never reconnects | Confirmed: the event socket is connected only once, and the error handler only logs ([`connection.cpp`](https://github.com/quickshell-mirror/quickshell/blob/1a4716cde794a59928d9d9fc15f2afc7a95de360/src/wayland/hyprland/ipc/connection.cpp#L63-L115)). Current Quickshell master is unchanged. |
| The matched line is what the shell logs | Confirmed: `Hyprland event socket error` is emitted only by that error handler. The "disconnected" and "Unable to connect" lines do not match. |
| The restart starts on the first match | Confirmed: in follow mode, `journalctl` exits when its stdout reader goes away ([`journalctl-show.c`](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/781d9d0789379d1ea1f2ecefb804d41e9c8b6c38/src/journal/journalctl-show.c#L448-L475)), so the pipeline finishes as soon as `grep -m 1` matches, without waiting for another log line. `-n 0` does not replay older errors. |
| `setsid -f` keeps the restart alive, and the `EXIT` trap cleans up otherwise | Confirmed in an isolated fixture: the restart ran detached and outlived the launcher, exactly one restart ran, and on `TERM` no watcher processes remained. |

### A restart refused under the lock screen is not retried

The watcher fires once, and `omarchy-restart-shell` [refuses to run](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/e50f773275cf82f689614f65d7262bcd53e15556/bin/omarchy-restart-shell#L29-L35) while the session lock is secure or requested. The PR description names heavy work at resume as a trigger, and Omarchy locks before suspend, so resume is exactly when the lock is up:

```text
socket dropped while locked
  -> watcher: grep -m 1 matches, pipeline ends
  -> setsid -f omarchy-restart-shell   (output to /dev/null)
       -> "Refusing to restart Omarchy shell while the session is locked." exit 1
  -> watcher is gone; the old shell keeps running with a closed event socket
user unlocks
  -> no new socket error is logged, nothing retries
  -> bar stays stale until a manual `omarchy restart shell`
```

An isolated fixture with a stub restart that refuses showed the same sequence: the watcher processes were gone after the refusal, the old shell kept running, and a second error line started no new attempt. The refusal itself is unchanged at the merge-base and on current `quattro`; the new part is that the automatic one-shot call depends on it.

**Impact:** in the resume case the PR describes, the bar stays stale after unlock, the same as before the change. The restart's output goes to `/dev/null`, so the refusal leaves no trace in the journal.

**Suggested change:** keep the watcher armed until a restart actually runs, for example by waiting until `omarchy-hyprland-session-locked` reports unlocked before calling `omarchy-restart-shell`. Logging when the watcher fires (with `logger -t omarchy-shell`, as the launcher already does for relaunches) and sending the restart's stderr to the journal would make a refused or failed restart visible.

### The watcher reacts to any shell's log line, not only its own

The watcher filters on the `omarchy-shell` tag only, and every launcher uses that tag. Nothing ties a match to this launcher's shell. With two Omarchy shells for the same user, for example a nested Hyprland session running the Omarchy autostart, one socket error fires every watcher. Each restart then runs `quickshell kill -p "$CONFIG_DIR" --any-display` ([`omarchy-restart-shell` L66](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/e50f773275cf82f689614f65d7262bcd53e15556/bin/omarchy-restart-shell#L66)), which also stops the other session's shell when it shares the config path. In the isolated fixture, an error entry written under the tag by an unrelated PID triggered the restart.

**Impact:** single-session desktops are unaffected. In a multi-session setup, a socket drop in one shell restarts both, and the concurrent restarts are not serialized.

**Suggested change:** match only this shell's entries, for example `journalctl --user -f -n 0 -o cat _PID="$shell_pid"`, with the watcher started per `run_shell` iteration (`systemd-cat` execs Quickshell, so the stream PID is the shell's PID).

**Optional test improvement:** `test/shell.d/launch-shell-test.sh` and `test/shell.d/restart-shell-test.sh` stub `quickshell`, `systemd-cat` and `hyprctl` but not `journalctl`, so every launcher they start now follows the real user journal and could reach the installed `omarchy-restart-shell`. A `journalctl` stub in both tests restores their isolation, and a launcher case where the stub emits the error line would cover the one-shot trigger, the detached restart and cleanup on `TERM`. These are the relevant suites for the launcher; the PR description cites `./test/cli`.
